description: The HGVS recommendations' own worked normalization examples — rows where the spec names an input and prints, in the same sentence, what the description must be instead. Two rules are covered: the coding-sequence restriction on repeat notation (repeat units must be a multiple of 3, with the UTRs carved out) and the 3'rule's exon/exon-junction exception. Both are sequence-dependent, so neither can fire in the harvested spec fixture, which normalizes through an empty MockProvider. Here they run against real reference bases served from the committed hermetic slice beside this file. Each row is pinned under all three shipped input-hygiene modes, because they do not agree and which mode produces which answer is itself the finding.

cases.note: A 1-nt repeat unit on a coding reference: not a multiple of 3, so the repeat spelling is unavailable and the spec prints the dup form to use instead. Ferro converts it, in every mode.

A 2-nt repeat unit on a coding reference: same restriction, and the spec prints the insertion form to use instead. STRICT MODE REJECTS THE SPEC'S OWN INPUT: the reference tract at c.1738 is not a whole number of TA copies ('expected TA[k] (k whole copies), found T (1 bp; unit_len 2 does not divide span)'), so a mode that refuses to repair a reference mismatch cannot reach the prescribed answer. Recorded as observed behaviour, not endorsed — nobody has adjudicated whether strict mode should accept an input the spec publishes.
The other half of the same sentence: the prescribed form is itself a fixed point. Without this row a normalizer that rewrote the answer into some third spelling would still satisfy the row above.
Fixed-point half of the insertion row — and note it is accepted in strict mode, unlike the repeat spelling of the same variant.

citation.quote: As such, `NM_024312.4:c.-6_-3G[6]` is valid as the reading frame is not affected.

cases.note: The carve-out, and the row that makes the two above meaningful: the restriction is scoped to the coding sequence, so a 1-nt repeat unit in the 5'UTR keeps its repeat spelling. A normalizer that simply refused all short repeat units on a `c.` reference would pass the CDS rows and fail here.
The RNA axis carries the same restriction, stated separately in RNA/repeated.md.
RNA counterpart of the 2-nt unit row, and it inherits the same strict-mode rejection — the tract it names is the same one.
Fixed-point half of the RNA dup row.
Fixed-point half of the RNA insertion row.

citation.quote: the format r.-125_-123cug[4] should not be used; it contains redundant information

cases.note: THE ONE DIVERGENCE, and it is a spec self-conflict rather than a ferro defect. `RNA/repeated.md:22` marks range-plus-unit invalid as redundant — the range `-125_-123` already fixes the unit — while `:27` publishes `NM_024312.4:r.-6_-3g[6]`, exactly that shape, as valid. The two cannot both hold, and ferro answers BOTH WAYS depending on input-hygiene mode: the plain library path leaves the published form alone, lenient strips the redundant label (W3013) and emits `r.-6_-3[6]`, strict rejects the input outright. So the divergence lives in the preprocessor's repair, not in the normalizer. All three answers are pinned rather than reconciled: this is the spec's conflict to settle, not ferro's. Recorded as the undecided ruling `rna-repeat-range-plus-unit-redundancy` in tests/fixtures/grammar/hgvs_spec_normalization_overrides.json, and owed upstream via #466.

citation.quote: the variant is described as `LRG_199t1:c.3921dup` (`NC_000023.10:g.32459297dup`) and not as `c.3922dup`

cases.note: The flagship worked example of the 3'rule's exon-junction exception (`general.md:44`), and the direction the exception is normally tested: c.3920=A, c.3921=T, c.3922=T, so the unrestricted 3'rule would shift this dup across the junction into the next exon. It must not, and does not. See the sibling row for the direction that is NOT asserted.

citation.quote: the variant (`NC_000023.11:g.32441180dup`) is **not described** as `c.3922dup` since this would shift the position of the variant to the next exon

cases.note: `spec_expected` WAS NULL AND IS NOT ANY MORE, and that is the whole change here. c.3921 and c.3922 are both T, so at the transcript level `c.3921dup` and `c.3922dup` denote one sequence — yet ferro emits two fixed points, and they project 2,790 bp apart (`LRG_199:g.903430dup` vs `g.906220dup`, matching the spec's own `g.32459297dup` vs `g.32456507dup`). The field was null on the reasoning that the spec published no answer for this input. It does, three times, independently: `duplication.md:26` names c.3921dup as THE description and says the variant is not described as c.3922dup, `:60` restates that on the GRCh38 coordinates, and `:148` gives the reason — translating c.3922dup back to a genomic position lands at the wrong nucleotide, in the wrong exon. The ruling `exon-junction-dup-converge-from-the-far-side` is now DECIDED: CONVERGE, so this row is a recorded DIVERGENCE — ferro's three outputs below are today's behaviour and none of them is the spec's answer. #1621 closes the gap; when it lands, all three become `LRG_199t1:c.3921dup` and the row stops diverging.
